title: SBA run context (resolved configuration)
description: The single effective configuration for one run: the output of the resolver, written to context.json in the run-state store, and the only technical input the roles receive. Produced from the business contract plus the catalogue, for GCP on GitHub Actions. Three properties are load-bearing and are the reason this document is a schema rather than a generated file. One, it is complete: every value a role needs is present, so a role never consults the catalogue, the request, or the clock, and stage re-entry works because a stage can reconstruct everything from this document alone. Two, it is deterministic: given the same contract and the same as_of, byte-identical output, which is what makes order-independence and the CONFIGURATION_DRIFT_IN_RUN check provable. Three, it is closed: additionalProperties is false at every level, so a role cannot be handed a field the resolver did not intend. See AD-03, AD-22, docs/architecture/configuration-resolution.md section 4, and docs/architecture/cloud/gcp.md.

schema_version.description: Semantic version of this schema, not of the contract. Incremented with the document shape, and used by the resolver and the roles to detect a context written by a different release. See AD-20.

catalog_version.description: Version of the configuration tree that produced this document, so a golden-file diff attributes a change to a catalogue edit rather than to a code edit. Recorded on the run result as code.catalog_version. See docs/architecture/configuration-resolution.md section 5.

as_of.description: The instant the resolution is evaluated against, RFC 3339 UTC. This is the resolver's ONLY time input, and it is an argument rather than a clock read: that is what keeps the resolver pure under AD-22 and what makes a golden file reproducible. It governs image expiry and change-freeze windows. A wall-clock stamp such as generated_at is deliberately absent -- the caller may add one, but the resolver must not, because a resolver that reads the clock cannot be proven order-independent. See docs/architecture/configuration-resolution.md section 10 and AD-22.

identity.description: Who and what this run is. The only part of the document derived from the request; everything else is catalogue.

request_id.description: Echoed from the contract. The idempotency key and the run-state prefix. See AD-04 and AD-05.

correlation_id.description: Generated by the caller and propagated into every log line, every label and every artifact. A UUIDv7 so that lexical order is chronological, which makes the run-state prefix listing sortable without an index. See docs/api/api-contract.md section 4.3.

run_id.description: Identifies this execution attempt as distinct from the request. A re-run of the same request_id gets a new run_id and an incremented attempt, which is how a resumed run is distinguished from the original. See docs/architecture/idempotency.md section 5.

application.description: Resolved application code, upper-cased as it arrived. The application record is what supplies the project, the network tier, the cost centre and the owner.

environment.description: Resolved environment. Selects the policy floor, the GitHub Actions environment and its approval gate, the GCP project, and the identity federation subject. A production identity must be unreachable from an untrusted ref; that boundary is enforced by the OIDC trust policy and this value is what it is written against.

provider.description: Lower-case provider key, matching sba_provider_capabilities.name in configuration/clouds/gcp.yml. Lower case because this is the key the TagMapper and the capability declaration are indexed by, and it is not the value the contract carries.

cloud.description: Upper-case provider name as it arrived in the contract, retained for correlation with the request and the result artifacts.

region.description: Business region code, echoed from the contract. Retained so an operator reading the context does not have to open the request to know which footprint was requested.

gcp_region.description: The concrete GCP region resolved from configuration/regions/, e.g. europe-west1. Distinct from identity.region so that a business code is never passed to a provider module. See AD-19.

os_family.description: Lower-case OS family, the key the OS catalogue and the baseline roles are indexed by.

roles.description: The role names the playbook dispatches to. Emitted by the resolver from a closed map keyed on identity.provider, never interpolated from request data, because a caller-influenced role name is arbitrary code execution with extra steps. This is AD-08 expressed in the document. See docs/architecture/provider-abstraction.md section 1.

cloud_role.description: The instance lifecycle role. Present in roles/cloud/, and statically named in the playbook's import_role list; the playbook branches on this value with a when guard rather than performing a dynamic include.

image_role.description: The image resolution role. Present in roles/image/.

tag_mapper.description: The TagMapper that projects the canonical key set onto GCP labels and annotations. One implementation per provider, so the label and annotation rules live in one place. See AD-11 and docs/architecture/configuration-resolution.md section 8.

placement.description: Where the instance is created. Every value here is immutable after creation on GCP, which is why verify_immutable asserts this whole block and converge_instance must never write to it. See docs/architecture/cloud/gcp.md section 4.

project_ref.description: The GCP project, by reference rather than by id, so the platform never carries a project number. Resolved from the environment and the application footprint. Least privilege is expressed as a binding on this value in the workload identity trust policy. See docs/architecture/cloud/gcp.md section 8.

zone.description: The GCP zone, e.g. europe-west1-b. Immutable after creation, and not available in every region -- a zone absent from configuration/regions/ for the target region must fail at resolution with REGION_NOT_AVAILABLE, never at apply. Distribution across zones for a batch is a capacity decision, not a resilience one; see zone_semantics and docs/architecture/cloud/gcp.md section 2.

zone_semantics.description: A declaration, not a value: it records that a GCP zone is a deployment locality with NO capacity-isolated failure-domain guarantee, so the requester-facing surface must not present zone choice as a resilience control. Carried in the document so the property travels with the decision rather than living only in prose where a future change could quietly drop it. Const rather than enum, because this is the honest value and pretending to offer an isolation guarantee would be promising something GCP does not provide.

zone_selection.description: How a multi-server batch is spread across the region's zones. first_available avoids a single zone's capacity limit without claiming fault isolation. Absent for a single-server batch.

network_ref.description: The VPC network name. Referenced, never created by a build: the platform references networking and does not create it, because subnet and IP capacity are managed outside the platform and a build that could allocate a Private Service Connect range could exhaust it for the whole estate. See docs/architecture/cloud/gcp.md section 6.

subnet_ref.description: The subnet name the instance's single attached interface goes into. The NIC is attached at create and cannot be added afterwards without stopping the instance, so this is immutable. Free-address capacity for the requested count is checked at pre-flight and is not retryable within a retry window.

service_account_ref.description: The service account attached to the instance, if the role needs one. Attached at create and used for guest OS features and workload identity. Never a key: a key file is a long-lived secret, and none exists anywhere in this platform. Omitted when the role needs none.

private_google_access.description: Whether Private Google Access must be satisfied by the referenced subnet. A pre-flight assertion, not a setting the build changes: a subnet without it routes egress through the public path, bypassing the organisation's egress controls. See docs/architecture/cloud/gcp.md section 6.

external_ip.description: Whether an external IP is attached. Always false in this release: an external address on a production server is a finding in most baselines, and a build that could request one would make that baseline opt-out. Widening this is a catalogue and policy change, never a contract change. See docs/architecture/cloud/gcp.md section 6.

compute.description: Instance shape. Split from placement because machine type and disk shape are the mutable half: machine type can be resized without a reboot, while disks have their own rules. converge_instance writes only within this block and never shrinks a disk. See docs/architecture/provider-abstraction.md section 3.2.

machine_type.description: Fully qualified machine type, e.g. zones/europe-west1-b/n2-standard-4. Fully qualified rather than short because the short form is region-ambiguous and an unqualified machine type is a common source of a machine that does not exist in the chosen zone. Resizable in place without a reboot, so this is a converge target rather than an immutable attribute. A type unavailable in the target zone is SIZE_NOT_AVAILABLE_IN_REGION and must fail at pre-flight, because discovering it at apply leaves an orphaned half-created instance.

os_disk.description: Boot disk. On GCP the boot disk is created with the instance unless a pre-created disk is attached; either way its size and type are fixed by the image and the PD type cannot be changed on an attached disk, so a type change is a rebuild rather than a converge.

size_gb.description: Boot disk size in GiB. Expandable, but on GCP that requires deallocating the instance first, so the platform reports it as a reboot-equivalent event rather than a silent in-place change.

type.description: Persistent disk type. Immutable on an attached disk, so a change here is a rebuild, not a converge.

kms_key_ref.description: Cloud KMS key resource name for CMEK encryption, or null when the project default key applies. A reference, never key material; the platform identity needs only cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter on this key. Null is permitted but a regulated workload's policy floor will reject it, which is the correct place for that decision. See docs/architecture/cloud/gcp.md section 1 and docs/security/secret-management.md.

auto_delete.description: Whether the disk is deleted with the instance. True for the boot disk, which is what makes decommission leave nothing behind.

data_disks.description: Data disks, attached at create. Expandable only; a shrink is never performed, because data on the far side of a shrink is unrecoverable and AD-16 retains rather than destroys. An empty array is the normal case and is not the same as absent.

name.description: Disk name, derived from the instance name so a disk is traceable to its instance by name alone during an incident.

size_gb.description: Data disk size in GiB. Expand-only; the resolver will not emit a smaller value than the live disk, and converge must never shrink.

type.description: Persistent disk type. Immutable on an attached disk.

device_name.description: Guest-visible device name, e.g. /dev/disk/by-id/google-scsi-0. Fixed by the role and the OS family, not by the requester.

kms_key_ref.description: Cloud KMS key resource name for CMEK, or null for the project default key. A reference, never key material.

auto_delete.description: Whether the disk is deleted with the instance. True: a retained instance must not leave an unattached billable disk behind, and AD-16 retains the instance rather than stranding its data.

accelerators.description: Attached accelerator devices. Empty in this release; the catalogue has no entry that requests one, and a GPU attached to the wrong machine type fails at apply in a way that is awkward to recover from. Reserved so that adding one is a catalogue change and not a schema change.

count.description: Number of accelerators. Bounded because it is a scarce, quota-governed resource.

image.description: The resolved image. Every field here is chosen by the catalogue and pinned; the request cannot influence any of it. Resolution failures are IMAGE_NOT_FOUND, IMAGE_NOT_APPROVED, IMAGE_EXPIRED and IMAGE_REVOKED, and all four are non-retryable because a retry cannot make an image appear or unexpire. See docs/architecture/configuration-resolution.md section 7 and docs/architecture/cloud/gcp.md section 5.

catalog_id.description: The catalogue entry this resolved from, e.g. ubuntu-2204-standard. The key an operator greps for when asking which approved image a fleet was built from.

provider.description: Provider that owns the image. Always gcp in this release.

project.description: Project that owns the image, distinct from the target project. The build identity needs roles/imageReader on this project, which is a narrower grant than on the target project and is the reason it is named separately.

image.description: The exact image name, pinned. Never a family and never latest: a moving reference makes a build non-reproducible and makes a no-op re-run report OS_VERSION_MISMATCH, because the idempotency check compares the current image against the recorded one and a family will have moved. latest is excluded structurally rather than by convention, because latest is syntactically a valid image name and so would pass any pattern -- a convention is not enough when the failure only surfaces as a mismatch on every subsequent re-run. See AD-07 and docs/architecture/cloud/gcp.md section 5.

self_link.description: The resolved self link the module actually receives, so the recorded value is unambiguous rather than a reference the platform would have to re-resolve. Recorded next to the family so a DescribeImage comparison is exact. See docs/architecture/cloud/gcp.md section 5.

family.description: The image family, recorded for the DescribeImage comparison and for describe calls. Recorded, never used as the reference to create from.

build_date.description: Build date of the pinned image. Carried so a CVE window can be evaluated against the image rather than against the OS version string, which does not change when an image is rebuilt.

baseline.description: The CIS benchmark version applied by the security role, e.g. cis_linux_2025_1. Derived from the image and the environment, never from the request, and the single field that makes compliance evidence attributable to an image rather than to a run. See docs/architecture/role-dependency-model.md.

pinned_at.description: The as_of at which this pin was resolved. Makes an expiry evaluation auditable: the run used the image that was valid then, and an image that expired since does not retroactively invalidate the run.

guest_os_features.description: Guest OS features requested, e.g. SEV_LAUNCH for confidential computing or UEFI_COMPATIBLE. Empty in this release. Each feature has hardware and machine-type preconditions, so a feature that cannot be satisfied is a pre-flight assertion against the resolved machine type -- SEV_LAUNCH on a machine type without SEV is INDETERMINATE_AT_PREFLIGHT rather than a late apply failure. See docs/architecture/cloud/gcp.md section 1.

naming.description: Names and instance identifiers, produced by the naming engine. One entry per requested server, and the order is the creation order. short_name is bounded to 15 characters because it becomes a NetBIOS computer name, which is a hard platform limit and not a platform convention; fqdn must be globally unique within the DNS scope. See AD-06 and docs/architecture/configuration-resolution.md section 6.

pattern.description: The pattern used, with the resolved placeholders, e.g. {app_code}-{env_code}-{role_code}-{region_code}-{seq:03d}. Carried so an operator can see the rule, not only its output -- a name nobody can explain is a name nobody can extend safely.

dns_scope.description: The DNS zone the FQDNs are registered in, checked at resolution for uniqueness across the scope. A collision with an existing A record is DNS_RECORD_CONFLICT and is never auto-resolved, because the record points at a live address and overwriting it could take a service offline. See docs/architecture/failure-and-retry.md section 4.2.

instances.description: One entry per requested server. The length of this array equals the requested count and is a useful cross-check: a resolver that emitted fewer or more entries than the request asked for has a bug that the schema cannot catch, so the resolver's unit tests assert the invariant.

index.description: 1-based creation order within the batch. Also the disambiguator in the naming pattern. See A-38.

short_name.description: NetBIOS computer name, at most 15 characters. This is a hard limit in the directory, not a platform preference, and a property test asserts no catalogue combination can produce a longer value. Resolved to lower case because AD and NetBIOS are case-insensitive while GCP instance names are not, and one canonical case is what makes the two systems agree on which object is which.

fqdn.description: Fully qualified name, unique within dns_scope. Property-tested for syntactic validity and uniqueness across the catalogue.

sba_instance_id.description: The golden join key: a UUID assigned before anything exists and written as a label in the same call that creates the instance. One value correlates the request, the run state, the GCP label, the IAM condition, the DNS record and the CMDB CI. It is the only design in which create-or-adopt, per-run least privilege and cross-system correlation all work, and it is why the lookup is by label and never by name. See AD-05 and docs/architecture/idempotency.md section 4.

zone.description: The zone this instance is placed in. Present per instance rather than once on placement because a multi-server batch can be spread across zones, and because zone is immutable -- a distribution decision that changed between runs would be an IMMUTABLE_MISMATCH on the adopted instance.

os_build.description: In-guest configuration the OS baseline role applies. Populated for both families; the fields that do not apply to the resolved os_family are simply absent rather than null, so a role never has to branch on a null it should not see. Re-running os_config must produce changed == 0. See docs/architecture/idempotency.md section 3.

update.description: Whether the role applies OS updates during the run. True by default; a catalogue entry may disable it for an image that is updated by other means.

packages.description: Package names to install. Names only: a repository, a version pin and a checksum come from the enterprise package repository the role reads at run time, so that a package cannot be sourced from an arbitrary location by a catalogue edit. See docs/architecture/execution-environment.md.

features.description: Windows features to enable or disable, e.g. NetFx3, SMB1Removal. Present only for the windows family.

sysctl.description: Kernel parameters to set, as a name to value map. Present only for the linux family.

time_sync.description: The time source. A cross-stage dependency worth naming explicitly: an unsynchronised clock breaks domain join, which fails with an error that does not mention time at all, so this is resolved rather than left to a distribution default.

winrm_port.description: WinRM listener port for the windows family. Bound at resolve time because a port that is wrong is a connection timeout whose message names nothing useful.

winrm_transport.description: WinRM transport. ntlm-in-tls where the enterprise baseline permits it and kerberos where it does not; the role asserts the listener matches this value rather than trusting the image.

ssh_port.description: SSH listener port for the linux family. See winrm_port for why this is resolved rather than defaulted at run time.

local_admin_pattern.description: Pattern for the local administrator account, e.g. adm-{short_name}. A pattern and not a name because the account must be derivable by an operator from the server name alone during an incident. The account's credential is never in this document, is rotated away from the image default in the same run, and is stored only in the secret store. See docs/architecture/failure-and-retry.md and docs/security/secret-management.md.

security.description: Security baseline and required agents. See docs/architecture/role-dependency-model.md and docs/security/security-architecture.md.

baseline.description: The CIS benchmark to apply, matching image.baseline. Kept here as well because security.baseline is what validate_os asserts against, and an assertion that reads a different field from the one that was applied cannot fail correctly.

policies_applied.description: Every policy file that contributed a value to this run, e.g. production, enterprise, cis_windows_2025_1. The audit list on the run result, and the answer to 'which floor applied' without re-deriving it.

required_agents.description: Agents the server_role requires. A closed enum, because install_agents maps each to a role and an unknown agent would have nowhere to go. An agent that installed but has not yet heartbeated is AGENT_NOT_REPORTING and is retryable -- treating it as fatal would fail builds that produced correctly configured servers, and because AD-16 retains infrastructure would create a PARTIAL over an entirely healthy estate. See docs/api/api-contract.md section 3.2.

shielded_vm.description: Whether Shielded VM is required, satisfied by secure boot and vTPM on the image plus the guest OS features requested. A pre-flight assertion, because the two mitigations are only meaningful together and enabling one alone is worse than enabling neither, since it advertises protection that is not there. See docs/architecture/cloud/gcp.md section 1.

monitoring.description: Monitoring policy the monitoring_agent role applies. See docs/architecture/role-dependency-model.md.

policy.description: Named monitoring policy, resolved by the role from the management platform at run time. A name, not a configuration blob, because a monitoring policy is owned and reviewed by the operations team and duplicating it here would create a second copy that drifts.

check_interval_s.description: Check interval in seconds. Bounded, because the role registers this with the management platform and an absurd value would be a denial-of-service against it.

enforcement.description: Whether the host is expected to be reporting by the end of enroll_agents. False for a decommissioning run, where requiring a heartbeat from a server being removed would fail the teardown.

backup.description: Backup policy the backup_agent role applies. See docs/architecture/role-dependency-model.md.

policy.description: Named backup policy, resolved by the role from the backup platform at run time. A name rather than a configuration blob, for the same reason as monitoring.policy.

schedule.description: Backup schedule, e.g. nightly. A closed set: an arbitrary schedule string reaching a backup platform is a way to request a schedule nobody reviewed.

retention_days.description: Retention in days. Bounded below by the compliance floor, which a policy file enforces rather than this schema; the schema bounds it to stop an unbounded integer reaching the backup platform.

dns.description: DNS registration, applied per healthy host. Deliberately after domain join and agent enrolment, so a name is only resolvable once the host can answer, and a failed earlier stage does not publish a name that resolves to nothing. See docs/architecture/request-lifecycle.md.

zone.description: The delegated zone the records are written to. Must equal naming.dns_scope; the resolver asserts the two agree, because a name registered in one zone and a record written to another produces a host that resolves nowhere while both stages report success.

primary_record.description: Which name the A record carries. Always the FQDN in this release; the field exists so that a future PTR-first or alias-based scheme is a catalogue change rather than a code change.

ttl.description: Record TTL in seconds. Bounded low deliberately: a 3600-second TTL would make the dns stage the slowest in the run for no benefit, because these records are expected to be stable. See A-21.

ptr_record.description: Whether a reverse record is created. Required by the baseline and asserted by dns, since a host resolvable forward but not reverse fails several directory and monitoring lookups in ways that are hard to diagnose later.

domain.description: Directory join target. On-premises Active Directory is the assumption behind this block (A-04); a managed identity answer would change the domain_join role, the validate_os assertions and the retry profile, and would require a domain_provider dimension here. See docs/assumptions.md section 7.

name.description: The DNS domain to join, matching the DNS zone. Resolved from the environment, not from the request.

ou.description: The OU the computer object is created in, as a distinguished name. Catalogue-driven per application, never hard-coded in a role: a hard-coded OU means every new application needs a code change, which is precisely what the catalogue exists to avoid. See OQ-13.

join_account_ref.description: Reference to the directory join credential in the secret store, resolved to its value at the moment of use with no_log set. A reference and never a value: extra-vars are logged, run state is retained, and anything placed in this document would be disclosed by both. See AD-15 and docs/security/secret-management.md.

workgroup.description: The pre-join workgroup for the Windows single-domain join path. Bounded short because NetBIOS limits it to 15 characters, the same hard limit as short_name and for the same reason. See AD-06.

cmdb.description: CMDB record the servicenow_cmdb role upserts, keyed on sba_instance_id. One CI per healthy host. See docs/architecture/logical-architecture.md.

class.description: The CI class, e.g. cmdb_ci_computer. Named rather than hard-coded per role, so a different CMDB class is a catalogue change. See A-08.

assignment_group.description: The group that will own the record and receive its alerts. Resolved from the application's ownership record, which is a separate catalogue file precisely because ownership changes on an org-chart cadence and application technical configuration does not. See docs/architecture/configuration-resolution.md section 5.

correlation_field.description: The CI field carrying sba_instance_id, e.g. u_sba_instance_id. Named rather than assumed, because the upsert keys on it and a wrong field would produce a duplicate CI on every run instead of an update. A duplicate is detected as CMDB_DUPLICATE_DETECTED. See docs/architecture/idempotency.md section 7.

metadata.description: The canonical key set projected onto GCP labels and annotations. This block is AD-11 paid for. labels are the enforcement copy -- 63 characters per key and value, lower case, [a-z0-9_-], usable in a gcloud filter, countable in a billing export, readable by an IAM condition, and settable only at creation. annotations are the complete copy, unbounded and case-preserving, mutable without a restart. The two are kept identical by one TagMapper function, and every divergence between them is recorded in transformations rather than applied silently, because a silent truncation discovered later in a cost report cannot be explained. See docs/architecture/cloud/gcp.md section 3.3.

labels.description: The GCP labels, written in the create call. sba_instance_id is required in this set and not merely conventional: without it as a label, per-run least privilege is impossible on GCP, because IAM conditions can read labels and not annotations, and create-or-adopt would find nothing on a re-run. Key and value patterns are the API's, enforced here so a violation is a resolution error naming the key rather than a 400 from the API. See docs/architecture/cloud/gcp.md section 8.

annotations.description: The complete metadata, written immediately after create and then verified by a read-back. Values here are unbounded and may be mixed case, which is what allows a data classification such as PCI-DSS Cardholder Data to be recorded faithfully when its label form would be rejected. See docs/architecture/cloud/gcp.md section 3.1.

transformations.description: Every place where a canonical value could not be represented as a label, and what was done about it. Empty when labels and annotations are identical. The entries surface in the golden resolution files, so a change to the label rules shows up in a pull request as a one-line reviewable diff rather than as a cost report three months later. Ordered application: truncate to 63, then strip characters outside [a-z0-9_-], then if the value is empty omit the label and keep the annotation -- a placeholder is worse than an absence, and the API rejects an empty label. See docs/architecture/cloud/gcp.md section 3.3.

key.description: The canonical key that could not be represented as a label.

to.description: Where the value was placed instead. Always annotation in this release: a value that cannot be a label cannot be truncated into one, and rewriting it to a lossy form would put a wrong value in the enforcement copy.

reason.description: Why. Carried as a closed enum rather than prose so that a new reason is a schema change that gets reviewed, and so a golden-file diff reads as a cause rather than as a sentence.

original_length.description: Length of the canonical value before transformation, so a reviewer can see whether a truncation occurred without opening the catalogue.

lifecycle.description: How this run should behave for the current attempt. See docs/architecture/idempotency.md section 5 and docs/architecture/failure-and-retry.md.

stage.description: The stage this invocation should run, or the empty string meaning the full stage sequence. Stage dispatch is by variable and not by playbook (AD-01), so a single stage is re-runnable in isolation against durable state without re-running its predecessors. The enum is the closed set that makes the stage table statically enumerable for --list-tags and for the requester-facing stage list. See docs/architecture/role-dependency-model.md.

attempt.description: 1-based attempt number for this run. Incremented on resume, and the input to the retry policy. A domain credential failure does not increment it into a retry, because a retry would multiply failed logons and could lock the service account. See docs/architecture/failure-and-retry.md section 4.2.

on_failure.description: What happens to infrastructure created by this run when a later stage fails. Always retain: destroying would orphan the directory object, the DNS record and the CMDB record, and would destroy the diagnostic evidence, so the platform forward-fixes instead. This is a const rather than an enum because a build that auto-destroyed would need a reviewed compensating path for every resource type, and none exists. See AD-16.

batch_serial.description: The serial batch size from the policy floor. Prod is 1: a multi-server serial batch that is interrupted leaves some servers built and some not, and the half-built set is the harder case to reason about. 1 means a failure leaves a clean boundary. See docs/architecture/idempotency.md section 6.1.

stages_completed.description: Stages already recorded as complete in the run state for this request. The input to stage re-entry: a stage re-runs only what its guard says is incomplete, which is why a re-run of one stage does not re-provision. See AD-01 and AD-04.

policy_evaluation.description: The result of the policy gate, computed at resolution. A policy can only make a resolved configuration illegal, never different, which is why adding a policy file can never silently change what a server looks like. See docs/architecture/configuration-resolution.md section 10.

rules_evaluated.description: How many policy rules were evaluated. Recorded so a zero-violation result is distinguishable from a gate that did not run, which are otherwise the same empty object.

violations.description: Rules that failed. A non-empty array is POLICY_BLOCKED and the run must not proceed. A violation names the rule, not a free-text message, so a requester-facing message can be built from a template and never from an exception. See docs/architecture/configuration-resolution.md section 10 and docs/api/api-contract.md section 3.1.

rule.description: The policy rule identifier, e.g. prod.requires_backup.

message.description: A message built from a closed template set. Never a raw exception and never a value from configuration that could be sensitive, because this text reaches a requester-facing surface. See docs/api/api-contract.md section 3.1.

path.description: The resolved path the rule evaluated, so an operator can find the value without searching. See docs/api/api-contract.md section 3.1.

advisories.description: Rules that passed with a warning. Non-blocking by design, and reported so a warning is never silently dropped: a rule that can never fail is a rule nobody reads.

message.description: A message from the closed template set.

preflight.description: The live checks run at the validate stage, appended as they execute. An array rather than a map so that a finding can be addressed by index in an error's detail_source -- context.json#/preflight/13 -- which keeps the requester-facing response small and stops the detail itself leaking topology. The checks are read-only and run under the read-only half of the split identity: pre-flight must not be able to create anything, so that a pre-flight failure is guaranteed to have created nothing. See docs/architecture/role-dependency-model.md and docs/security/security-architecture.md section 3.1.

check_id.description: The check identifier, e.g. gcp.subnet.free_addresses or gcp.machine_type.available.

status.description: The check outcome. A warn still permits the run and is reported; a fail blocks it. There is no skip: a check that could not run is fail, because a check that silently does not run is how a build reaches production with an unverified precondition.

check_class.description: Which identity the check ran under. A read-only assertion must not be reachable by an identity that can write, and recording the class here is what makes that auditable rather than assumed. See docs/security/security-architecture.md section 3.1.

message.description: A message from the closed template set, e.g. Subnet snet-payments-prod-app has 1 free address; 2 requested. Never a raw API error, which routinely embeds a project number, a zone and a quota name. See docs/api/api-contract.md section 3.1.

error_code.description: The error code this check maps to when it fails, so the check and the registry cannot disagree. A failed capacity check is SUBNET_IP_EXHAUSTED, which is deliberately not retryable: a quota does not restore itself inside a retry window, so retrying is pure delay. A rate limit is a different condition and is retryable. See docs/architecture/failure-and-retry.md section 2.

remediation_ref.description: Reference to a change record, request or catalogue entry the requester would need in order to resolve the finding, e.g. a subnet range extension. A reference and never an instruction to open one, because the platform does not create change records.

provenance.description: Where each resolved value came from, as a flat list of path-to-source entries. This is the reason a policy rejection is explainable to a requester: a rejection names a rule, and the rule names a value, and this says which catalogue file and precedence level produced that value. An array of entries rather than a map keyed by path, because a map would have to leave additionalProperties open at exactly one level, and a schema that tolerates unknown fields anywhere is a schema that will eventually accept something dangerous. See docs/architecture/configuration-resolution.md section 4 and AD-22.

path.description: The dotted or indexed path of the resolved value, e.g. compute.machine_type or naming.instances.0.zone. The same path syntax detail_source uses, so an operator follows one convention rather than two.

source.description: The catalogue file that produced the value, relative to the configuration root, e.g. server_roles/application.yml. A path into the repository and never an absolute filesystem path, which would leak the runner layout into a shared artifact. See docs/api/api-contract.md section 10 on message sanitisation.

level.description: The precedence level, lower to higher, matching docs/architecture/configuration-resolution.md section 4. Policies are level 0 and are a floor rather than a source of values, so a path whose level is 0 was constrained by a policy rather than given by one. Recording the level is what lets a reviewer see that a value came from the request and not from an override nobody noticed.

value_hash.description: A hash of the resolved value rather than the value itself. Sufficient to detect drift between two resolutions of the same contract -- which is all the idempotency check needs -- without duplicating every value into a second structure that could disagree with the first. See docs/architecture/idempotency.md section 2.

resolved_config_hash.description: A hash over the whole document, excluding resolved_config_hash itself. The value on the run result and the callback, and the mechanism by which an auditor confirms that a stored context and a reported result correspond without the topology leaving the run-state store. See docs/api/api-contract.md section 5.2 and docs/architecture/request-lifecycle.md section 7.1.

immutable_after_create.description: The GCP attributes that cannot be changed after creation, recorded here so verify_immutable and the documentation cannot drift apart. An instance whose project, region, zone, network, subnet, image or attached-disk type differs from this document is IMMUTABLE_MISMATCH, and correcting it means a rebuild rather than a converge -- a rebuild is a new run, never an in-place fix. See docs/architecture/provider-abstraction.md section 3.2 and docs/architecture/cloud/gcp.md section 4.
